_about: Side-chain and terminal pKa values used by the Henderson-Hasselbalch charge
These are measured literature values for model compounds, not fitted scoring
coefficients, which is why they live here rather than in the policy artifact:
they are shared, citable and the same for everyone. What the policy does own
is the burial shift applied on top of them (chemistry.burial_pka_shift), which
Each entry records the spread across commonly cited sources, because that
spread is the honest uncertainty on any charge computed from it. Where the
spread is wide the value is marked context_dependent, and anything drawn from
it should be reported as approximate rather than as a determined number.

source.primary: Model-compound pKa values as tabulated in standard biochemistry texts (Nelson & Cox, Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry; Berg, Tymoczko & Stryer, Biochemistry).
source.note: Values for free amino acids in water at 25 C. A residue inside a peptide, and especially inside a folded structure, can differ substantially.

H.note: The one side chain that titrates inside the physiological-to-endosomal window, so its assumed pKa drives any pH-switching conclusion.

C.note: Strongly perturbed by local environment; active-site cysteines can fall below 5.

n_terminus.note: Varies with the identity of the first residue.

c_terminus.note: Varies with the identity of the last residue.
